questions.question: A model receives audio and produces written words. Which modality path describes Whisper?
options: Text tokens through encoder to a waveform vocoder
Audio waveform through a speaker classifier
A transcript through a patch embedding layer
Log-mel audio through encoder to text decoder
questions.explanation: Whisper converts audio into log-mel frames, encodes those frames, and autoregressively decodes text tokens. A vocoder would synthesize speech from text, which is the reverse direction of this recognition path.

questions.question: At 16 kHz, what sample counts correspond to Whisper’s 25 ms frame and 10 ms hop?
options: 25-sample frame and 10-sample hop
400-sample frame and 160-sample hop
160-sample frame and 400-sample hop
800-sample frame and 320-sample hop
questions.explanation: At 16,000 samples per second, 25 ms is 0.025 × 16,000 = 400 samples and 10 ms is 0.010 × 16,000 = 160 samples. The 160/400 option reverses frame duration and hop stride.

questions.question: What role does Whisper’s convolutional stem play before the transformer encoder?
options: It replaces the log-mel input with codec tokens
It assigns speaker labels to each transcript word
It converts encoder states back into a waveform
It down-samples the log-mel frame sequence
questions.explanation: The convolutional stem reduces the log-mel time-frame sequence before self-attention, shortening the sequence the encoder processes. Speaker labels and waveform generation are separate tasks and are not the stem’s function.

questions.question: Which prompt prefix requests French input speech to be translated into English?
options: French language tag with the translate task token
English language tag with the no-timestamps token
French language tag with the transcribe task token
English language tag with the transcribe task token
questions.explanation: The prompt’s French language tag identifies the source language, and the translate token requests translation into English. The transcribe token instead asks for the words in the identified language.

questions.question: A meeting transcript must include speaker identities and turns. Which limitation should the system address separately?
options: Whisper converts each transcript token into an embedding label
Whisper’s 30-second window automatically clusters speakers
Whisper assigns speaker labels through its translation token
Whisper has no diarization, so add a speaker diarization tool
questions.explanation: Whisper performs transcription but does not determine who spoke each segment; diarization requires a separate component such as pyannote. A 30-second input window sets chunk length and does not automatically cluster speakers.

questions.question: A deployment needs low-latency live transcription on an edge device. Which choice fits the lesson’s model-selection guidance?
options: Use a dedicated streaming or edge ASR model
Send each turn to Whisper as a 30-second batch
Use a waveform vocoder to predict text tokens
Use a BERT encoder with a sentiment head
questions.explanation: The lesson distinguishes Whisper’s fixed 30-second chunks from native live streaming, and recommends dedicated streaming or edge ASR for low latency. Submitting each turn as a 30-second Whisper batch preserves the limitation.
